headline: Maui County Committee on the Status of Women

meeting.body: Maui County Committee on the Status of Women
meeting.summary: Staff confirmed enough members were present to hold the meeting.
meeting.recap: Staff confirmed enough members were present to hold the meeting.[[0:02:09]] No one signed up to testify.[[0:03:56]] The Hawaiʻi State Commission on the Status of Women has hired an executive director who starts December 6th.[[0:04:15]] She said the timing would connect to the August 8th wildfire commemoration.[[0:12:56]] Members voted to approve the recommended budget for fiscal year 26.[[0:32:32]] A second vote let the chair review the final draft and send it to the mayor.[[0:33:54]] Survey feedback from the last conference was deferred to January.[[0:38:11]] A county lawyer said the state office that enforces open meeting rules has been leaning toward keeping things public.[[0:52:41]] The lawyer said they would ask that office about using letters instead of award nominee names.[[0:57:32]] The chair said a man told her the hospital maternity ward has only eight rooms.[[1:07:52]] A member suggested self-care and self-esteem as a topic for women.[[1:11:43]] The next meeting's agenda was set for January 21st.[[1:18:12]] Staff said the March meeting moves from the 18th to the 27th.[[1:18:28]]
decided: Members voted to approve the recommended budget for fiscal year 26.
Members voted to let the chair review the revised budget and send it to the mayor.
The committee chose not to form a permitted interaction group for event assignments.
meeting.next: A member will bring a plan for the wellness forum, including who is involved, in January. The county lawyer will put the question about anonymous nominees on a to-do list and send an email. Members can send more topic ideas to be compiled.
